title: CDrus Expression
description: Defines an Expression in the CDrus language. An Expression specifies an intent — build, deploy, verify, and so on — by declaring the CDEvents that together fulfill that intent. Every Expression is bound to an identity tuple: (group, author, expression). The identity is the commitment; Expressions do not carry versions. A change to the boundary semantics of an Expression requires a new identity (a new expression name, or transfer to a different author or group). Internal refinements that preserve the boundary contract retain the same identity. Expressions compose: a composite Expression references other CDrus Expressions as constituents by identity. Per-event field requirements live in the CDEvent schemas themselves (using one-way inheritance for vendor-specific extensions), not in the Expression.

group.description: Group component of the Expression's identity tuple. MUST be a registered group name in the processing service's group index (e.g., 'payment-engineering', 'prod-sres', 'data-platform', 'identity-services', 'risk-analytics'). Lowercase, hyphen-separated. The group is the organizational unit within the enterprise; it is what scopes authorship and authorization for the Expression.

author.description: Author component of the Expression's identity tuple. MUST be a registered user name in the processing service's user index. The author is the engineer whose intent this Expression encodes; ownership of the Expression — including responsibility for what should happen, what failure looks like, and how to respond when expectations diverge — is bound to this identity. Lowercase, hyphen-separated.

expression.description: Expression component of the identity tuple (e.g., 'build', 'deploy', 'verify', 'build-deploy', 'integration-test'). The full identity is the tuple (group, author, expression). The canonical file naming pattern is <group>.<author>.<expression>.expression.yaml. Lowercase, hyphen-separated.

description.description: Human-readable description of the intent this CDrus Expression captures.

produces.description: Ordered list of CDEvents and/or sub-Expressions that together fulfill this CDrus Expression. Order is significant: events fire depth-first in the order specified — a parent event with nested produces fires, all its descendants fire (recursively), then the parent's next sibling fires. Sub-Expressions are expanded recursively at the position they appear, resolved by identity. A list element may also be a concurrent branch (a nested list): sibling branches run concurrently and the parent does not complete until every branch has completed.

produce_item.description: A produce item is one of three mutually exclusive forms within a single item: (1) a CDEvent (terminal, optionally with nested produces and/or detach lists); (2) a reference to another CDrus Expression by identity (composition, no nesting); or (3) a concurrent branch — a nested list of produce items that runs in PARALLEL with its sibling branches in the same list (see 'concurrent_branch'). The three forms are structurally distinct: an event item and an expression item are objects; a concurrent branch is an array.

concurrent_branch.description: A concurrent branch: an ordered sub-sequence of produce items (events, sub-Expressions, or further nested branches) written as a nested YAML list. Like a detached branch (an event's `detach` entry), a concurrent branch is its own chain with its own chainId, linked to the spawning event by a RELATION link; the only difference is one bit — the parent WAITS on a concurrent branch. Sibling concurrent branches run concurrently; their events are the output — there is no join, merge, or synthetic join event — and the parent chain does not reach COMPLETE until every concurrent branch has completed (a branch that never completes leaves the parent incomplete). Sibling concurrent branches whose event sequences are identical are legal and expected (e.g. parallel test-case runs under one suite) and are disambiguated by their distinct chainIds, not by content.

event_item.description: An event item references a CDEvent type to emit. It may carry a nested produces list (events triggered by this event, fired in depth-first order before the next sibling) and/or a detach list (detached branches spawned by this event, each with its own chainId and RELATION link back; the parent does not wait for them). A produces or detach entry may itself be a concurrent branch (a nested list) — the awaited parallel counterpart of a detached branch.

event.description: CDEvent type to emit. CDEvents themselves are versioned by the CDEvents specification — distinct from CDrus Expression identity, which is unversioned. Multiple forms are accepted and resolve identically: (1) canonical embedded-version form 'dev.cdevents.build.started.0.1.1' (exact match); (2) colon form 'dev.cdevents.build.started:0.1.1' (exact match, equivalent); (3) no version 'dev.cdevents.build.started' (resolves to latest available); (4) colon-separated semver range 'dev.cdevents.build.started:^0.1.0' (resolves to highest matching). Standard semver range syntax applies — caret, tilde, x-ranges, and explicit ranges (the last must be quoted in YAML). Vendor-specific event extensions are referenced by their full extended type string. Detailed semver-range validation occurs at resolution time. Linters may normalize between the canonical and colon forms.

event_schema_uri.description: URI to the event's JSON Schema. Optional; consumers may fall back to local schema lookup when not provided.

produces.description: Events triggered by this event, fired depth-first in the order specified. All produced events share the parent's chainId. The parent's next sibling does not fire until every descendant has fired.

detach.description: Detached branches spawned by this event. Each gets its own chainId at run time, with a RELATION link from the parent event to the first event of the branch. The parent does NOT wait for a detached branch to complete; its next sibling fires immediately. Detached branches are declared (not implicit) so consumers can act as a babysitter — tracking expected branches, raising alerts if they fail to start or hang. Without an explicit detach declaration, an unrelated chain spawned in the runtime is unobservable to the system. For the awaited counterpart (the parent blocks until the branch completes), write a concurrent branch — a nested list — instead.

expression_item.description: An expression item references another CDrus Expression by identity. Expressions are identified by the (group, author, expression) tuple. References use path-style notation and may be fully qualified or abbreviated when the processing service can resolve the missing components from the current processing context. The referenced Expression is resolved and expanded recursively at run time. Expression items cannot carry produces or detach lists — those properties belong on the events the referenced Expression itself produces, in the referenced Expression's own definition.

expression.description: Reference to a sub-Expression by identity, in path form. Three reference forms are supported, from least to most qualified: 'build' (resolved within the current group and author context, e.g., when both referrer and referent share the same group and author); 'mchen/build' (explicit author within the current group context); 'payment-engineering/mchen/build' (fully qualified identity). The processing service resolves abbreviated references against the current processing context. All path components follow the same lowercase-hyphen pattern.
